rationale.conceptual: The method applies a well-established periodic DFT protocol (B3LYP-D3, pob-TZVP, counterpoise BSSE) with vibrational and conformer corrections. No novel algorithm, but correct execution demands domain knowledge of lattice energy definitions, dispersion corrections, and basis set superposition errors; multiple components must be combined accurately.
rationale.execution: The workflow has many stages: retrieving crystal structures from CSD, gas-phase DFT optimization, conformational energy calculation, nine separate periodic DFT optimizations, vibrational frequency calculations for solid and gas, BSSE counterpoise corrections, and final arithmetic combination into two CSV files. Dependencies across steps are high, and the agent must drive a specialized code (CRYSTAL17) reliably.

difficulty.reasoning: The task is a multi-step periodic DFT workflow to reproduce lattice energies and sublimation enthalpies from the literature. The method is standard in computational chemistry (B3LYP-D3 with BSSE corrections), but requires careful implementation of several interacting components. The pipeline involves external data retrieval, gas- and solid-phase optimizations, conformer searches, vibrational calculations, and multiple corrections. Execution complexity is high due to orchestration of a specialized periodic DFT code and many interdependent steps.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The studied crystals are small (unit cells with few tens of atoms) and the basis set is moderate; the periodic DFT code used (CRYSTAL17) runs on CPU and requires only modest memory.
